newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Santander gets 90 pct Bco Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Santander gets 90 pct Bco Venezuela.

text.p: Spanish banking group Santander said on Tuesday it had been awarded a 90 percent stake in Banco de Venezuela for $338.4 million.
Earlier from Caracas the Spanish bank was said to have been awarded an 80 percent stake in the Venezuelan bank in a public auction for $301.1 million.
A statement from Santander in Madrid said that only 10 percent of the bank would be held by small investors, instead of 20 percent.
Banco de Venezuela had a net worth at September 30, 1996 of $248 million at current exchange rates and first nine months 1996 net income of $84 million, the statement said.
It was awarded to Santander at 1.51 times book value and the purchase will generate goodwill of $114 million.
"We are very pleased with this transaction. Banco de Venezuela is, without doubt, a great franchise with enourmos potential," Santander chairman Emilio Botin said.
"This investment forms part of our strategy of expansion in Latin America."
